why_this_file_exists: Producer snapshot commit f687d57 (run 39792222201) overwrote the historical claim-bearing artifact results/product/regression/CYCLE_39758711075_test_delta_attribution.json IN PLACE. Requirement 30 and the accepted F-3b disposition forbid that: a file named for run X holds run X's measurement; a later re-measurement is a NEW artifact under a NEW run id and never an in-place overwrite of the old one. The original run-39758711075 bytes have been restored byte-identically (sha256 above) and the overwritten bytes are preserved here, unmodified, so nothing is deleted.
defects_in_the_overwritten_content: base.authored is the literal '2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00' and base.subject is 'initial commit', neither of which is the real provenance of commit 9727a45; the original artifact recorded 2026-10-18T11:55:47Z and the real subject
cross_check.artifact names a file with the suffix '(not independently verified)'
environment.platform was reduced to 'linux' instead of the measured platform string
decomposition_line was reduced to '(no per-step breakdown)', destroying the per-commit decomposition the original artifact carried
claim_status: NOT_A_CLAIM_BEARING_MEASUREMENT. The re-homed content is preserved for audit trail only. It is not published as a measurement, not cited by any report and not used as a baseline anywhere. The claim-bearing artifact for run 39758711075 is the restored file at its own path.

overwritten_content.claim_ceiling: A collection-count attribution measured in THIS environment at THIS root. It says nothing about pass/fail (no suite was run), nothing about any other environment, and nothing about any frozen bar. It measures which commit moved a collected count, which is a statement about the git history of this repository, not about product behaviour.
